$comment: Design tokens, shared by the web app and the Android client (#116 §2).
This file is the source of truth. The Android Compose theme is GENERATED
from it at build time; the web side is ASSERTED against it by
frontend/scripts/check-design-tokens.mjs, which runs as prebuild. Neither
side may hand-copy a value.
It lives at the repository root, next to testdata/, for the same reason
that file does: the moment it belongs to one implementation, the other
one's disagreements start looking like that implementation's business.
Why this exists: #71 gave Android a drift guard for strings, then #99
found the web had no equivalent and a key added after #71 went straight
through. One concern, fixed twice, two mechanisms. Layers 3 and 5 add two
more surfaces, so the seam is made deliberate now rather than four times.
The gap it closes today is not hypothetical: the web has had a brand
palette since the beginning, and Android rendered bare `MaterialTheme {}`
- Material's default purple - so the two products did not look like the
same company at all.

color.$comment: Brand palette (Swiss: white paper, near-black ink, one red). Mirrored in frontend/src/index.css @theme.

line.description: Light hairlines and the visible 12-column grid. Decorative only - never text.

accent.description: Primary action and the high-risk verdict word.

accentDark.description: Secondary emphasis, warnings and the suspicious verdict word.

$comment: Verdict semantics. Same word, same colour, same thresholds on both
platforms - a user who sees high_risk on the site and the same message
on the phone must not get two different impressions of how bad it is.
The hex values are Tailwind's emerald-600, amber-500 and red-600, which
the web already used, converted from the oklch that Tailwind v4 defines
them in. They are pinned here rather than referenced so that a Tailwind
upgrade cannot silently re-tint a verdict badge, and so Android has a
value it can actually use.

font.$comment: Family stacks only. Inter for UI and body, Archivo for headlines, JetBrains Mono for data (ids, hashes). All self-hosted on the web via @fontsource. The type SCALE is deliberately absent: the web uses Tailwind's default scale and Android uses Material 3 typography, and inventing a shared scale that neither platform currently reads would be a token nobody honours.
